title: Dijkstra's shortest paths
summary: Shortest paths with weighted edges using a priority queue.
hints:
Keep `std::vector dist(n, INF)` with `dist[start] = 0`, and a min-heap of `(distance, vertex)` pairs: `std::priority_queue, std::greater

> pq;` where `P = std::pair`. Remember from the heaps exercise that the default priority_queue is a *max*-heap.

Loop: pop `(d, u)`. If `d > dist[u]` this entry is stale (a better route was found after it was pushed): `continue`. Otherwise relax each edge `(v, w)` of `u`: if `dist[u] + w < dist[v]`, set `dist[v]` and push `(dist[v], v)`.

Never add to `INF` itself (that can overflow). It is safe here because you only expand vertices you popped, whose `dist` is finite. For `dijkstra_path`, also keep `parent[v] = u` whenever you improve `dist[v]`, then walk back from the target and reverse, exactly like in the unweighted exercise.
